verdict.rationale: Reflect's own AI features let users switch between external models (GPT-4o or Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and the reflect.app page mentions connecting your own provider API key with requests going directly to that provider. That is a thin first-party link between notes and external LLMs. However, the API explicitly cannot serve note contents because of end-to-end encryption, so external AI tools can only append or create notes, not read them. Zapier is a generic automation bridge, not an AI connector. Missing for 10: first-party connectors that let external AI tools or agents read and query notes, an AI plugin ecosystem, read access to note content via the API, and independent corroboration of the bring-your-own-key flow (the reflect.app claims also conflict with other docs describing the product).
